sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Adedamola Aregbesola & Thelma Araokanmi. 2023. A Sociolinguistic Profile of Legboic Languages of Cross River State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2023-001. Dallas: SIL International. vi+54 pp.

sources.note: Nothing about Leyigha: sect. 4 'Previous research' (pp. 6-7) says 'There has previously been very little direct data collection and documentation of these language groups' and cites only Thomas 1914, Dimmendaal 1978, Sterk's unpublished 1976-79 manuscripts (via Blench 2021 ms), Crozier & Blench 1976, Hansford et al. 1976, Bendor-Samuel 1989, Udoh 2019 for Leyigha; sects. 5.1.4/5.2.4/5.3.4 'Assiga' (pp. 7-10): 'We were unable to interview any speakers of Leyigha' / 'unable to attain permission to collect data among the Leyigha speakers' (p. 3). The phonetic-inventory section (6.3) covers Legbo…

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2014/2021. The Upper Cross languages: a comparative study. Ms. (Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation; 'Manuscript in preparation'; delivered to Glottolog as, 189 pp.)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only work with first-hand Leyigha (Assigha) data beyond 1914; a comparative wordlist drawn from Sterk's 1976-79 manuscripts, likely with tone-marked forms and possibly a phonology overview of the group; cited by ASJP and Glottolog. Not posted on rogerblench.info (the Internet Archive 2019/2024/2025 Upper Cross page lists only the Mbembe dictionary); site itself could not be reached by automated download.
